rv.q: The Legend of Davie McKenzie is less certainly constructed, and the interplay of the characters less spiky, for all its good humour and poignancy.
Directed by Jake Sleet, it rarely misses a beat, the laughs come easily and the suspense builds as the plot and the lads’ relationship begins to twist.
It is Sean Connor as an irrepressible Davie, however, who drives things with a charisma that makes you understand why Sean falls under his spell.

cn.t: A tragicomic portrait of working-class friendship earns warm reviews, with critics praising its balance of humor and pathos as it traces two fatherless friends from childhood through prison to a tragic end.
